Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. This neuron gives its highest values to common function-word / punctuation continuation tokens (a comma, " that", " the", the clitic "âĢĻve", an opening curly quote, a word-continuing "ter") in the middle of flowing narrative prose, while it is most suppressed on word-final subword pieces of names/nouns ("izing", "ward", "oller", " Language") right at the start of a document — i.e. it tracks generic mid-discourse connective positions rather than any semantic content.
